cases.title: Before the flop: the big blind still gets a turn
cases.prompt: A three-player table has a button, small blind and big blind, clockwise in that order. Blinds are 1 and 2. The button acts first. Try calling around, then try a different legal line.

worked.reason: The button adds 2, matching the live big blind.
The small blind adds only 1 to the 1 already posted. All three have now paid 2, but the big blind has not taken its turn.
The big blind checks its option. It could instead raise. Now the round ends and the flop can be dealt; the pot is 6.

cases.title: On the flop: a check can be followed by a bet
cases.prompt: The same three seats reached the flop with 6 in the pot. Payments on this new round start at zero. The small blind acts first. Try checking around, then restart and add a bet or raise.

worked.reason: Checking adds nothing and keeps the small blind in the hand.
The big blind opens betting for 4. This gives the small blind another decision, even though it already checked.
The button adds 4. The small blind still needs to respond.
The small blind matches the 4. Everyone remaining has responded to the latest wager; the round ends with 18 in the pot.

cases.title: Facing a raise: count only the new counters
cases.prompt: There was 6 in the pot before this flop round. The small blind bet 4, the big blind raised to 10 total, and the button folded. The small blind acts again. Try a call, then restart to compare a fold or a full raise.

worked.reason: The call adds 10 minus 4 = 6, making 26 in the pot. No earlier-street payment reduces this amount. A full raise would need to reach at least 16 total, adding at least 12 to the small blind's 4. The previous raise increased the wager by 6, from 4 to 10; it did not increase it by 10.
